stops.note: dutiful devotion to gods, country and family; Virgil's hero is 'pius Aeneas'
narrowed to compassion; the same Latin word, borrowed again, gave 'piety', and Italian gave the Pietà
Shakespeare's Othello (c. 1603) gives the word its most famous line: 'But yet the pity of it, Iago! O Iago, the pity of it, Iago!'

current_meaning: sorrow and compassion caused by others' suffering
